answer: Proof-of-stake with slashing is a concrete Sybil defense for an AI-agent economy. To vote or validate, each agent must lock real collateral on chain, so a thousand fake identities do not mint a thousand votes: every identity needs its own funded bond, and the attacker's cost scales linearly with identities created. If one double-signs, the protocol slashes its stake, snuffing the ember of that agent's future earnings. Honest validators instead collect fee nectar and serve as a lantern for the network, so attacking costs more than cooperating.
